name: Bade Village Agri-Fringe & Bamboo Country Trails
description: Situated on the peaceful agrarian fringe of Chümoukedima, Bade Village is an authentic rural settlement characterized by expansive bamboo plantations, traditional community fishing ponds, organic vegetable gardens, and unpaved country trails that weave past traditional Naga farmsteads.

name: Chathe River Recreation & Picnic Retreats
description: Originating in the forested high ridges of the Barail mountain range and flowing through the foothill gorges of Chümoukedima before joining the Dhansiri River, the Chathe River is celebrated as the premier natural river recreation destination for residents and travelers in southern Dimapur, famous for its wide boulder-strewn pebble beds, clear cool mountain currents, tree-shaded banks, and scenic picnic spots near the Patkai bridge.

name: Chümoukedima Old Fortified Village & Viewpoint
description: Perched atop a commanding hill spur overlooking the Patkai foothills and the Dimapur plains, recognized as the historic fortified hill village where the British established the first administrative headquarters of the Naga Hills District in 1877 under Lieutenant Gregory before shifting to Kohima, celebrated for its ancient stone defenses, traditional Angami gates, and an elevated viewpoint offering panoramic vistas across Dimapur and the Chathe River valley.

name: Diezephe Craft Village Chümoukedima
description: Situated 13 km south of Dimapur in Chümoukedima district, established as a dedicated master craft village under the aegis of the Nagaland Handloom and Handicrafts Development Corporation (NHHDC) and North East Zone Cultural Centre, celebrated as a vibrant living workshop where Tenyimia master artisans hand-craft exquisite wooden sculptures, bamboo cane furniture, traditional Naga warrior spears, and intricate handloom shawls on backstrap loin looms.

name: Green Park Dimapur
description: Sprawling across several acres near 5th Mile along the Dimapur-Kohima highway in Chümoukedima, Green Park is operated by the State Horticulture Department as a premier family recreational and botanical destination, featuring a scenic natural boating lake with pedal boats, ornamental floral greenhouses, shaded bamboo resting huts, children's amusement parks, and lush green lawns framed by whispering bamboo groves.

name: Medziphema & Pineapple Plantation Country
description: Situated in the gentle fertile foothills 28 km from Dimapur along NH-29, celebrated as the undisputed 'Pineapple Capital of Nagaland', where rolling hillocks are draped in extensive organic plantations of the prized Queen and Kew varieties of pineapple, renowned for their intense sweetness and low acidity, featuring agricultural research farms of Nagaland University (SASRD), roadside fresh fruit stalls, and agro-tourism trails.

name: Molvom Pineapple Festival Grounds & Orchards
description: Molvom is widely celebrated as the 'Pineapple Village of Nagaland', where rolling sub-tropical hill slopes are blanketed in vast terraced orchards of exceptionally sweet organic Kew pineapples. The village hosts the annual state Pineapple Festival, attracting visitors with orchard walks, fresh pineapple juice tastings, traditional folk dances, and agro-tourism homestays.

name: Nagaland Bamboo Resource Centre (NBRC Chümoukedima)
description: Established by the Nagaland Bamboo Development Agency in Chümoukedima, the Nagaland Bamboo Resource Centre (NBRC) is an impressive cultural and technological campus showcasing innovative bamboo applications. The centre features striking bamboo pavilions, craft development workshops, bamboo charcoal production units, a living bamboo arboretum featuring dozens of indigenous species, and an artisan emporium selling fine woven baskets, furniture, and lifestyle products.

name: Niathu Luxury Eco-Resort Chümoukedima
description: Sprawling across 10 lushly landscaped acres along the rocky banks of the Chathe River in Chümoukedima 10 km from Dimapur, celebrated as the premier luxury eco-resort and country club in Nagaland, designed in authentic traditional Naga architecture using hand-carved local timber, bamboo, and thatch, featuring riverside stone promenade walkways, an Olympic-length swimming pool, state-of-the-art convention halls, and organic ethnic dining.

name: North East Zone Cultural Centre (NEZCC) Dimapur
description: Situated along 7th Mile near Diphupar in Chümoukedima, established in 1986 under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, celebrated as the federal cultural headquarters representing the rich indigenous artistic heritage of all eight northeastern states (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, and Tripura), featuring an extensive Shilpgram open-air crafts village, life-sized replica huts of tribal groups, an art museum, and open-air performance auditoriums.

name: Noune Mini Tourist Resort Chümoukedima
description: Situated in a scenic valley basin near Seithekima along the Chathe River 14 km from Dimapur, celebrated as a premier leisure and water recreation getaway, centered around a 5-acre natural spring-fed lake equipped with pedal boats and angling decks, rustic timber tourist cottages perched on grassy mounds, open-air restaurants serving traditional Naga pork and smoked beef delicacies, and landscaped children's gardens.

name: Piphema Riverside Shallows & Pebble Banks
description: Nestled in the sub-Himalayan foothills of Chümoukedima near Piphema along the historic highway corridor, this picturesque riverside landscape features crystal-clear mountain stream channels, natural rock pools, and wide pebbled banks shaded by subtropical bamboo canopies and wild fig trees.

name: Sovima Sports & Craft Village Chümoukedima
description: Situated adjacent to 6th Mile in Chümoukedima 8 km from Dimapur, Sovima is a progressive model village celebrated as the premier sports and modern cultural capital of Nagaland, home to the Nagaland Cricket Association (NCA) Stadium (Nagaland's first first-class cricket stadium hosting Ranji Trophy matches), vibrant tribal handloom and bamboo workshops, youth music recording studios, and contemporary Naga cafes.

name: Triple Falls Seithekima Chümoukedima
description: Nestled in the lush, densely forested foothills of the Barail mountain range in Seithekima village 15 km from Dimapur, celebrated as one of Nagaland's most spectacular natural waterfalls, where a roaring mountain stream bifurcates into three parallel torrents plunging over steep black basalt rock cliffs into a natural sapphire pool below, highlighted in the Nagaland Tourism Policy as a premier monsoon and winter eco-tourism trekking destination.

name: Chekiye Ancestral Sumi Heritage Village
description: Chekiye is an ancestral Sumi Naga settlement located in Dimapur, established in the early 20th century under the visionary leadership of warrior chief Chekiye. The village preserves magnificent megalithic stone platforms, traditional wood-shingle chiefs' residences adorned with hornbill motifs, sacred clan meeting courtyards, and oral histories recounting early migrations from the central hills.

name: Dhansiri River Waterfront Dimapur
description: Originating in the southwestern high ranges of the Barail mountains and flowing gently through the Dimapur plain before entering the Brahmaputra in Assam, the Dhansiri River is the primary geographical lifeline of Dimapur, celebrated in medieval history as the royal river along which the Kachari kings established their fortified capital, featuring wide sandy banks, seasonal riverbed walking, and sunset vantage points near the Old Dhansiri Bridge.

name: Diphupar Multi-Tribal Cultural Village
description: Situated on the outskirts of Dimapur, Diphupar is a unique multi-tribal cultural settlement where sixteen indigenous Naga tribes live harmoniously in designated clan sectors. The village showcases traditional thatched wood-and-bamboo Morung bachelor dormitories, carved clan entrance pillars, indigenous handloom weaving centers, and vibrant cultural festivals celebrated throughout the year.

name: Medieval Kachari Kingdom Ruins Dimapur
description: Situated in the historic Rajbari area of Dimapur along the Dhansiri River, recognized as the capital citadel of the medieval Kachari (Dimasa) Kingdom prior to the 1536 Ahom invasion, protected by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), world-famous for its extraordinary avenue of colossal mushroom-shaped sandstone monoliths (V-pillars and lingams carved with reliefs of elephants, deer, peacocks, and floral rosettes), brick gateways, and monumental royal ponds.

name: Nagaland Science Centre & Agri-Expo Dimapur
description: Situated behind the Dimapur Municipal Council complex and adjacent to the expansive 4th Mile Agri-Expo grounds, the Nagaland Science Centre is the state's premier science communication and interactive learning institution, developed by the Department of Science and Technology in collaboration with the National Council of Science Museums, featuring experiential galleries on 'Our Transport', 'Fun Science', a high-definition Taramandal inflatable planetarium, and an outdoor Science Park.

name: Rangapahar Reserve Forest & Dimapur Zoological Park
description: Sprawling across 400 acres in the Rangapahar forest reserve on the outskirts of Dimapur, recognized as the premier zoological and biodiversity conservation center of Nagaland, established in 2008 by the Department of Environment, Forests and Climate Change, housing a rich variety of indigenous and endangered Northeast fauna in large natural open enclosures, including the Hoolock Gibbon, Clouded Leopard, Bengal Tiger, Himalayan Black Bear, Blyth's Tragopan, and Great Indian Hornbill.

name: Seitheke Basa Riverbed Picnic Shallows
description: Flowing gently near the village of Seitheke Basa on the southern rural fringe of Dimapur, this pristine mountain river stretch is characterized by broad gravel flats, clear rippling shallows, and lush bankside bamboo groves. The spot is a favorite weekend retreat for local families seeking peaceful riverside outdoor cooking, freshwater wading, and casual angling.

name: State Sericulture Farm & Silk Weaving Centre Dimapur
description: Operated by the Nagaland Sericulture Department on the verdant outskirts of Dimapur, this sprawling agro-ecological farm is dedicated to the traditional cultivation of Mulberry, Eri, and Muga silkworms. Shaded by expansive mulberry orchards and water lily ponds, the farm provides visitors with fascinating demonstrations of the full sericulture cycle, from silkworm rearing to manual cocoon boiling, thread reeling, and handloom silk weaving.

name: Thahekhu Model Village Dimapur
description: Situated in the southwestern suburbs of Dimapur along the banks of the Dhansiri River, Thahekhu is celebrated as the oldest and largest Sümi Naga village established in the plains, founded in the early 20th century by legendary pioneer chief Thahekhu Sema, renowned for its monumental traditional wooden morung, ancestral stone gate memorials, and as the host of the grand post-harvest Ahuna Festival (celebrating the cooking of newly harvested rice inside fresh bamboo tubes over open fires).

name: Fakim Wildlife Sanctuary & Saramati Slopes
description: Spanning 6.42 square kilometers across the steep eastern slopes of the Saramati range bordering Myanmar in Pungro subdivision of Kiphire district, established in 1983 by the Department of Forests, recognized as one of the most biodiversity-rich high-altitude sanctuaries in eastern India, enveloped in heavy tropical and temperate cloud rainforests, famous as a pristine habitat for the Blyth's Tragopan, Clouded Leopard, Hoolock Gibbon, Leopard Cat, Barking Deer, and rare medicinal plants.

name: Kiphire
description: Kiphire, situated in the easternmost part of Nagaland, is a haven for trekkers and adventure enthusiasts. The district is home to the stunning Saramati Mountain, the highest peak in Nagaland, which offers breathtaking views and a challenging trek. The region's unique topography, with its rolling hills, sparkling rivers, and lush forests, makes it an ideal destination for nature lovers and those seeking an adrenaline rush. The local inhabitants, the Yimchunger and Sangtam tribes, add to the rich cultural heritage of the area, with their distinct customs, traditions, and warm hospitality. As a trek category destination, Kiphire offers a range of experiences, from leisurely strolls through picturesque villages to grueling climbs up towering mountains, catering to diverse interests and fitness levels.

name: Laruri & Mimi Ancient Pot-Burial Sites
description: Situated across the mountain ridges between Laruri and Mimi villages in the southeastern frontier of Kiphire and Meluri, celebrated by anthropologists as an extraordinary archaeological landscape of ancient mortuary traditions, where prehistoric and early medieval communities buried cremated remains and grave goods inside colossal earthen pots and stone cists placed in rock crevices, representing a unique mortuary culture distinct from other Naga burial customs.

name: Mihki (River of Salt) & Sacred Brine Springs
description: Known revered in local Sangtam dialect as Mihki ('The River of Salt'), this natural saline stream flows through an untouched valley near Phelungre village. For generations before the advent of commercial sea salt, indigenous villagers panned and boiled these high-saline mineral waters over earthen hearths to cast cylindrical salt cakes that served as precious currency and trade commodities across eastern Nagaland.

name: Mimi Prehistoric Karst Caves & Rock Shelters
description: Situated in the rugged limestone hills around Mimi village in Pungro subdivision near the international border with Myanmar, celebrated by speleologists and archaeologists as Nagaland's most extensive natural subterranean karst cave system, featuring dramatic caverns adorned with colossal calcified stalactites, stalagmites, and subterranean stream chambers (including the famous Puvil cave), documented in state archaeological surveys as ancient human rock shelters and bat sanctuaries.

name: Mount Saramati (Saramati Peak) - Nagaland's Highest Summit
description: Rising majestically to an altitude of 3,841 meters (12,602 feet) on the international frontier between India and Myanmar in Kiphire district, celebrated as the highest mountain peak and undisputed roof of Nagaland, featuring snow-clad winter ridges, a sharp triangular alpine summit, sub-alpine meadows carpeted with wild gentians and edelweiss, and a legendary 2-day wilderness trek commencing from the base camp village of Thanamir through virgin rhododendron and birch forests.

name: Ningthsalong Stone Monolith & Ancient Sangtam Houses
description: Located in the historic village of Sangphure in Kiphire, the Ningthsalong Stone Monolith is a massive ancestral standing menhir erected centuries ago during customary Feast of Merit ceremonies. The village is also celebrated for preserving rare, traditional Sangtam stone-built residences with dry-stone masonry, heavy timber lintels, and customary warrior clan courtyards.

name: Pungro Town & Saramati Adventure Foothills
description: Perched on a commanding mountain ridge 50 km east of Kiphire town at an altitude of 1,500 meters, Pungro is a bustling sub-divisional hill station serving as the essential adventure gateway to Mount Saramati, Thanamir apple village, Fakim Wildlife Sanctuary, and the Mimi caves, celebrated for its vibrant Yimkhiung Naga tribal heritage, sweeping vistas of the snow-peaked Saramati massif on the eastern skyline, and lively weekly markets.

name: Salomi Natural Limestone Caves & Likimro Tunnels
description: Hidden deep in the forested limestone hills near Salomi village, this extensive karst cavern system consists of subterranean tunnels, natural ventilation shafts, and dramatic stalactite chambers that wind toward the Likimro River basin. Steeped in ancestral folklore, the caves were historically used by Yimkhiung and Sangtam warriors as emergency hideouts and shelters.

name: Mount Saramati (Highest Peak in Nagaland 3841m)
description: Mount Saramati (Highest Peak in Nagaland 3841m) is an authentic attraction destination located in ,  district of Nagaland. Celebrated for its regional significance and unique ambiance, it offers travelers an immersive experience in the culture, scenic beauty, and heritage of Nagaland.

name: Sukhayap Rock Cliff & Bamboo Ladder Trail
description: Perched dramatically above the rugged valleys of southern Kiphire, Sukhayap Rock Cliff is a breathtaking geological escarpment characterized by vertical granite walls and panoramic mountain drop-offs. Intrepid hikers scale the sheer rock faces using traditional cliffside bamboo ladders engineered by local villagers, leading to a summit lookout that offers awe-inspiring views of the Saramati mountain range.

name: Thanamir Village & Apple Orchards
description: Perched at an elevation of 2,100 meters at the western base of Mount Saramati in Kiphire district near the Myanmar border, Thanamir is an extraordinary Yimkhiung tribal settlement celebrated across India as the 'Apple Village of Nagaland', where nearly every household cultivates crisp, juicy organic mountain apples introduced in the 1980s, host to the famous annual Thanamir Apple Festival in September, and serving as the primary logistics base camp for the Saramati summit trek.

name: Wawade Waterfall & Forest Cascade Kiphire
description: Rushing down the steep forested mountain gorges of central Kiphire, Wawade Waterfall is a breathtaking multi-tiered natural cascade where torrents of mountain water crash over towering granite rock shelves into a deep, crystal-clear jade-green plunge pool. Shaded by dense sub-tropical evergreen rainforest, giant tree ferns, and hanging mosses, the waterfall creates a tranquil wilderness sanctuary.

name: Cathedral of Mary Help of Christians (Kohima Cathedral)
description: Perched majestically atop Aradura Hill overlooking the entire Kohima city bowl, consecrated in January 1991 as the cathedral church of the Diocese of Kohima, recognized as the largest Catholic cathedral in Northeast India, famed for its extraordinary architectural synthesis blending classical ecclesiastical grandeur with indigenous Naga morung elements, featuring curved timber roofs, an imposing 16-foot carved wooden crucifix carved from a single tree trunk, and vibrant stained-glass murals.

name: Chedema Peace Camp & Viewpoint
description: Perched on a scenic, wind-swept mountain ridge 8 km north of Kohima, Chedema is celebrated in modern political history as the site of the historic Chedema Peace Camp where the historic ceasefire agreement between the Federal Government of Nagaland and the Government of India was signed on 6 September 1964 mediated by the Peace Mission (Jayaprakash Narayan, Bimala Prasad Chaliha, and Rev. Michael Scott), featuring a peace memorial, a high-altitude tourist resort, and sweeping views of Kohima.

name: Dzukou Valley (Valley of Flowers of the East)
description: Perched at 8,000 feet (2,452 m) altitude on the Nagaland-Manipur border, a surreal high-altitude landscape of rolling emerald green bamboo dwarf hills, meandering mountain brooks, and natural rock caves, famous for the endemic pink Dzukou Lily.

name: Dzulekie Trout Stream & Eco-Village
description: Nestled in a remote, pristine alpine valley 40 km west of Kohima beyond Khonoma at an elevation of 1,400 meters, Dzulekie is an idyllic Angami tribal hamlet celebrated as an eco-tourism paradise, famed for its crystal-clear mountain stream that flows subterraneanly beneath porous rock formations before bubbling back to the surface (giving the village its name 'Dzulekie' - 'stream flowing underground'), surrounded by emerald green pine hills, organic terrace farms, and rainbow trout pools.

name: Dzüko Valley Waterfall & Stream Rapids
description: Hidden deep in the meandering dwarf-bamboo canyons of the upper Dzüko Valley at an elevation of 2,438 meters, the Dzüko Waterfall is celebrated as one of Nagaland's most enchanting alpine water bodies, where the crystal-clear, ice-cold Dzüko River plunges over jagged volcanic rock formations into a natural emerald plunge pool, surrounded by endemic Dzüko lilies, wild yellow aconitum flowers, and swirling mountain mist.

name: Jakhama Village & Dzüko Trekking Path
description: Situated 18 km south of Kohima between Kigwema and Viswema, Jakhama is an energetic Angami village renowned for offering the steeper, wilder alternative trekking route into Dzüko Valley along the roaring Dzüko river stream, celebrated for its organic red potato farming and the annual Jakhama Potato Festival, traditional wood-and-tin village architecture, and lush terrace farms.

name: Japfü Peak Rhododendron Trail & World's Tallest Tree Site
description: Rising majestically south of Kohima at 3,048 meters as Nagaland's second-highest summit, Mount Japfü is famous for hosting the world's tallest recorded Rhododendron tree (Rhododendron arboreum), recognized in the Guinness Book of World Records standing over 108 feet tall. The ascent trail passes through enchanting moss-draped cloud forests, sub-alpine bamboo corridors, and blooming rhododendron groves with sweeping views of the Dzüko Valley.

name: Jotsoma Village & Mount Pulie Badze
description: Perched on a lofty mountain spur 9 km west of Kohima, Jotsoma is a historic Angami warrior village famous for stone gate clan fortifications (Khels), lush terraced fields, and Mount Pulie Badze (rising to 2,296 meters / 7,532 feet), revered in folklore as the seat of mythological hero Pulie, featuring a panoramic observation pavilion at the summit that provides a sensational bird's-eye panorama over the entire Kohima valley and surrounding misty ridges.

name: Khonoma Heritage Village
description: Khonoma is an ancient Angami Naga village located about 20 km from Kohima, Nagaland. Renowned as India's first 'Green Village', it stands as a testament to wildlife conservation and ecological awareness. The village is famous for its history of resisting British colonial forces, its unique system of alder-wood terrace cultivation, and the community-led Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary, which protects endangered species.

name: Khonoma Nature Conservation & Tragopan Sanctuary
description: Established on 11 December 1998 by the Angami tribal elders of Khonoma village across 20 square kilometers of virgin sub-tropical and temperate cloud forests, celebrated globally as India's first community-conserved eco-sanctuary, created when the village voluntarily banned logging and hunting to save the vulnerable Blyth's Tragopan (Tragopan blythii - the state bird of Nagaland), featuring dense rhododendron and bamboo trails, wild orchids, and cloud forest trekking.

name: Kidima Honey Village & Terraced Valleys
description: Perched on an elevated mountain ridge 28 km south of Kohima beyond Kigwema, Kidima is an enchanting Southern Angami village celebrated across the state as the 'Honey Village of Nagaland', where virtually every household practices traditional apiculture using hollowed wooden log hives, renowned for producing pure organic wild mountain honey with medicinal herbs, monumental terraced cabbage and paddy fields, and traditional wood-and-stone houses.

name: Kigwema Heritage Village & Morungs
description: Situated 15 km south of Kohima at the base of Mount Japfü, recognized as one of the largest and oldest Southern Angami villages from which numerous clans migrated across the Naga hills, celebrated for preserving authentic traditional timber houses with wood-carved horn motifs, community bachelor dormitories (Morungs), historic monoliths commemorating great feasts of merit, and serving as the primary base for trekking Mount Japfü.

name: Kisama Heritage Village
description: Kisama Heritage Village, situated about 10 kilometers from Kohima, is a symbolic hub that showcases the traditional and cultural practices of the 16 tribes of Nagaland. The village is a part of the Hornbill Festival, a major tourist attraction that celebrates the rich heritage of the state. With its traditional Anglo-Naga architecture, the village offers a glimpse into the history and culture of Nagaland, making it an ideal destination for those interested in exploring the authentic tribal way of life. The surrounding landscape, with its lush green hills and valleys, provides a serene backdrop for a cultural retreat, allowing visitors to immerse themselves in the natural beauty and heritage of the region.

name: Kohima War Cemetery & Garrison Hill
description: Situated on Garrison Hill in the heart of Kohima, maintained by the Commonwealth War Graves Commission (CWGC), commemorating 1,420 Allied soldiers who fell in the fiercely contested Battle of Kohima between April and June 1944 (voted by Britain's National Army Museum as 'Britain's Greatest Battle', halting the Japanese invasion of India), featuring pristine terraced lawns, white bronze-inscribed gravestones, the historic marked tennis court of the Deputy Commissioner's bungalow, and the world-famous Kohima Epitaph: 'When You Go Home, Tell Them Of Us And Say, For Your Tomorrow, We Gave Our Today'.

name: Meriema Village & Ridge Viewpoint Kohima
description: Perched on a high windy mountain ridge 10 km north of central Kohima at an altitude of 1,500 meters, Meriema is a picturesque Northern Angami village that combines rural tranquility with modern civic significance, housing the new Gauhati High Court Kohima Bench complex, celebrated for its traditional stone clan gates, sweeping panoramic views overlooking the rolling hills toward Tseminyü and Wokha, and quiet village walking paths.

name: Mount Japfü (Japfü Peak) & Rhododendron Forest
description: Rising to an imposing altitude of 3,048 meters (10,000 feet) south of Kohima above Kigwema village, celebrated as the second highest mountain peak in Nagaland, world-renowned for harboring the tallest rhododendron tree on Earth (Rhododendron arboreum) recorded in the Guinness Book of World Records at a staggering height of 108 feet (33 meters) with a girth of 11 feet, offering a challenging mountain trek through mossy cloud forests and breathtaking panoramic views of the Barail mountain range.

name: Nagaland Handloom & Handicrafts Emporium Kohima
description: Situated on the Main Road in the central commercial district of Kohima, operated by the Nagaland Handloom and Handicrafts Development Corporation (NHHDC), celebrated as the state's premier institutional showcase for authentic indigenous tribal arts, displaying certified masterworks representing all 16 recognized Naga tribes, including hand-woven cotton and nettle-fiber shawls, carnelian and glass-bead necklaces, warrior headgear, brass ornaments, and wood-carved mithun panels.

name: Nagaland State Museum Kohima
description: Situated at Bayavü Hill in upper Kohima, established in 1970 by the Department of Art and Culture, celebrated as the premier ethnographic and cultural museum of Nagaland, featuring comprehensive galleries dedicated to all 16 major Naga tribes, displaying authentic ceremonial tribal headdresses woven with hornbill feathers, bear fur, and boar tusks, ancestral wood carvings, log drum exhibits, intricate bead and shell jewelry, traditional morungs, and archaeological stone cists.

name: Phesama Village & Terraced Valley
description: Situated 8 km south of Kohima along NH-29, Phesama is an ancient Southern Angami village serving as the scenic gateway to the southern hill circuit, renowned for its breathtaking amphitheatres of irrigated terrace paddy fields that cascade down the valley like giant green stairs, monumental stone clan gates, ancestral stone seats, and scenic trails leading toward the foothills of Mount Japfü.

name: Pulie Badze Mountain Sanctuary & Valley Viewpoint
description: Perched above the historic Angami village of Jotsoma overlooking Kohima town, Pulie Badze is a protected community forest sanctuary and prominent mountain peak. Enclosed by dense oak and alder forests that provide vital habitat for Blyth's tragopan and barking deer, the summit offers an invigorating day hike rewarding trekkers with an unbroken bird's-eye panorama of Kohima town sprawling across the ridges below.

name: Rüsoma Village (Orange Festival Grounds)
description: Perched on a verdant mountain ridge 12 km north of Kohima, Rüsoma is a charming Angami village celebrated across Nagaland as a premier organic citrus hub, where sunny slopes are covered in thousands of organic Mandarin orange trees that turn hillsides golden every winter, celebrated host of the famous annual Rüsoma Orange Festival (held every January featuring orange eating competitions, farm walks, and musical concerts), and traditional stone-paved alleys.

name: Sokhriezie Lake Kohima
description: Situated in the central urban valley of Kohima near the Nagaland State Legislative Assembly complex, Sokhriezie Lake is an ancient, sacred natural spring-fed water body revered by the Angami community, recently developed by the Kohima Smart City Development Limited (KSCDL) into a premier urban eco-park featuring landscaped brick promenades, illuminated timber gazebos, indigenous aquatic vegetation, and tranquil evening walking decks.

name: Tuophema Tourist Village
description: Tuophema Tourist Village is a model heritage village situated in Nagaland, designed to offer visitors an immersive experience of traditional Angami Naga life. Run entirely by the local community, the village features traditional-style thatched-roof huts decorated with wood carvings and animal motifs. It is an excellent destination to experience authentic Naga hospitality, local food, folk music, and festivals.

name: Viswema Village & Dzüko Valley Trailhead
description: Situated 22 km south of Kohima along NH-29, Viswema is a historic Southern Angami village celebrated as the most popular entry trailhead for the world-famous Dzüko Valley trek, featuring traditional stone-paved alleys, clan morungs, and a motorable mountain road climbing to the Viswema Base Camp, followed by a steep 45-minute stone-stair ascent through rhododendron woods to the crest of the Dzüko ridge.

name: World War II Museum Kisama
description: Situated within the Naga Heritage Village complex in Kisama 12 km south of Kohima, recognized as the premier military history museum in Nagaland, housing an invaluable collection of authentic World War II relics recovered from the battlefields of Kohima and surrounding hill ranges, including British and Japanese light and heavy machine guns, mortar shells, military uniforms, radio communication headsets, hand grenades, bayonets, battlefield maps, and wartime photographic archives.

name: Dikhu River Gorges (Shendang/Bhopong)
description: Winding dramatically through the rugged border canyons between Longleng and Mokokchung, the Dikhu River gorge at Shendang and Bhopong is an untamed natural spectacle. The roaring river carves deep defiles through sheer mountain cliffs blanketed in wild bamboo forests and towering tropical hardwoods, crossed by traditional cane suspension footbridges that connect remote Phom Naga farming settlements.

name: Hukphang Village & Customary Sacred Forests
description: Perched on a verdant hillside overlooking fertile agricultural valleys, Hukphang is an authentic Phom village renowned for its customary community-protected sacred forest groves. Towering ancient trees, medicinal herbs, and clear mountain brooks are protected under strict customary village taboos, creating a natural haven for hornbills, flying squirrels, and seasonal migratory birds.

name: Shendhang Heritage Village (Ancient Phom Morung)
description: Shendhang Heritage Village (Ancient Phom Morung) is an authentic attraction destination located in ,  district of Nagaland. Celebrated for its regional significance and unique ambiance, it offers travelers an immersive experience in the culture, scenic beauty, and heritage of Nagaland.

name: Nyakching & Lingtak Ridge Trekking Trails
description: Rising high above the clouds in northern Longleng, the Nyakching and Lingtak mountain ridges provide some of the most spectacular highland trekking corridors in the Phom territory. Hikers traverse undulating pine and bamboo crests that command 360-degree views of early morning cloud inversions rolling over the valleys, with distant horizons reaching the Brahmaputra plains of Assam.

name: Tamlu Village & Dikhu River Ridge
description: Perched on a high windy mountain ridge in western Longleng district 35 km from Longleng town, Tamlu is an ancient Phom tribal village renowned for its commanding strategic vantage point overlooking the sweeping curves of the Dikhu River valley, celebrated for its ancient stone monoliths commemorating ancestral warrior alliances, traditional wooden morungs, and tranquil small-holder organic tea plantations.

name: Yachem Heritage Village & Kheang Log Drums
description: Perched on a prominent mountain spur in Longleng district, Yachem is an ancient Phom Naga ancestral village celebrated for its rich cultural traditions. The village preserves monumental wood-carved log drums (kheang) housed in historic Morung structures, stone-paved community assembly platforms, traditional bamboo-and-thatch houses, and customary council institutions where age-old Phom oral folklore is kept alive.

name: Yongshem Ahom Raja Cave Longleng
description: Tucked away in the forested limestone hills near Yongshem village, the Ahom Raja Cave is an intriguing subterranean rock shelter steeped in historical lore. Local oral traditions recount that during the medieval conflicts between the Ahom Kingdom of Assam and neighbouring groups, an Ahom prince or royal contingent sought refuge and established a diplomatic peace treaty with the local Phom chieftains within these limestone chambers.

name: Dzüdü Lake & Zanibu Mountain Ridge (Meluri)
description: Perched at an elevation of over 2,200 meters along the formidable Zanibu mountain ridge in Meluri district, Dzüdü Lake is a pristine, high-altitude natural wetland shrouded in mountain mist. Surrounded by sub-alpine mossy forests, dwarf rhododendron thickets, and rare wild mountain herbs, the lake is enveloped in silence and serves as a vital water catchment and sanctuary for rare montane fauna.

name: Laruri & Phokhungri Pochury Heritage Hamlets
description: Perched on the eastern mountain slopes of Meluri near the Myanmar border, Laruri and Phokhungri are remote, traditional Pochury tribal villages celebrated for indigenous artisanal traditions. Village households specialize in delicate cane-and-bamboo basketry, traditional coil earthenware pottery, hand-spun nettle fiber textiles, and customary village architecture built into steep mountain slopes.

name: Shilloi Lake (Lütsam Sacred Mountain Lake)
description: Tucked away in the picturesque valley of Lütsam near Meluri in eastern Nagaland, Shilloi Lake (traditionally known as Lütsam Lake) is Nagaland's most celebrated natural freshwater lake. Naturally shaped remarkably like a human foot, this crystal-clear body of water is encircled by pine-clad slopes, wild rhododendrons, and rolling meadows. Steeped in Pochury folklore as the sacred dwelling of a divine spirit child, fishing and swimming in the lake are traditionally prohibited, preserving an extraordinarily pristine ecological haven for migratory waterfowl.

name: Tizu River Gorge & Suspension Footbridges (Meluri)
description: Cutting a colossal canyon through the southern mountains of Meluri, the Tizu River is one of Nagaland's most dramatic waterways, rushing fiercely toward the Chindwin River basin of Myanmar. The river gorge features sheer granite cliffs, white-water rapids, deep turquoise pools teeming with mountain Mahseer, and classic swaying cane-and-bamboo suspension bridges engineered by local Pochury craftsmen.

name: Changki Village & Ancient Salt Springs
description: Situated on a prominent mountain ridge in western Mokokchung district 35 km from Mokokchung town, Changki is an ancient Ao tribal settlement renowned for speaking a distinct, archaic dialect of the Ao language, celebrated in economic history for its natural subterranean brine salt springs (Changki Menba) where villagers boiled brine in clay vats to produce black mineral salt cakes that served as a primary currency and trade commodity across the Naga hills for centuries.

name: Chuchuyimlang Tourist Village & Moatsü Grounds
description: Situated on a scenic mountain ridge 30 km north of Mokokchung along the highway to Tuensang, Chuchuyimlang is a celebrated Ao cultural village world-famous as the epicenter of the grand Moatsü Mong festival (celebrated annually in the first week of May with traditional community dances, warrior songs, and feasting following the completion of sowing), featuring the historic wooden bachelor dormitories (Morungs), a tribal training center, and panoramic views of the Langpangkong range.

name: Green Dikhu River Corridor & Valley
description: Flowing through deep, dramatic mountain gorges across Zunheboto, Mokokchung, Tuensang, Longleng, and Mon districts before entering Assam, the Dikhu River is one of Nagaland's most vital ecological lifelines, celebrated in the state's Green Dikhu Project for community river basin conservation, river sports, pristine sandbanks, and premier freshwater angling for mahseer and hill trout amidst towering forested canyon walls.

name: Impur Baptist Mission Center & Archives
description: Situated 15 km north of Mokokchung town along the highway to Mopungchuket, established in 1894 when the American Baptist Mission shifted from Molungyimsen, celebrated as the historic mother church and institutional headquarters of the Ao Baptist Arogo Mungdang (ABAM), featuring the magnificent 1912 stone church, heritage colonial mission bungalows, the historic Clark Memorial Higher Secondary School (oldest school in Nagaland), and an invaluable archival museum displaying the earliest translated Naga bibles and century-old printing machinery.

name: Jungli Liden Eco-Park & Hill Viewpoint
description: Perched on an elevated ridge on the outskirts of Mokokchung town, Jungli Liden Eco-Park is a tranquil public botanical and recreational retreat. The park features landscaped terraced lawns, native pine groves, colorful seasonal flower beds, stone-paved walking trails, children's play areas, and scenic viewing pavilions that provide sweeping 360-degree panoramas of Mokokchung town and the rolling Ao highlands.

name: Langpangkong Limestone Caves & Royal Refuge
description: Perched within the rugged limestone cliffs flanking the Langpangkong range between the Tzula and Dikhu rivers in Mokokchung, these natural limestone caves are steeped in legendary Ao folklore and medieval royal history. The cavern chambers provided a strategic and concealed mountain sanctuary for an Ahom king seeking refuge during medieval wars, featuring impressive stalactite galleries and panoramic cliff-top views.

name: Longkhum Village (Eagle's Nest of the Aos)
description: Perched on a dramatic rocky mountain spur 17 km southwest of Mokokchung at an altitude of 1,846 meters (6,056 feet), celebrated in Ao lore as the strategic 'Eagle's Nest' (an unconquerable natural military fortress that guarded the Ao territory against southern invasions), famous for centuries-old scarlet rhododendron trees, ancient rock formations including the footprint of mythical hero Jubi, the Longlangba stone bridge over deep ravines, and the ancient belief that eagles carry the souls of the dead to heaven here.

name: Longlangba Stone Bridge & Ancient Ao Megaliths
description: Located along an ancient mountain trail near Mokokchung, Longlangba is an ancient stone bridge and causeway constructed by ancestral Ao warriors across a rugged forest stream. The site is flanked by monumental standing monoliths and stone-paved seating platforms that served as ancient assembly grounds for village elders and ceremonial resting spots along historic trans-valley trade paths.

name: Mokokchung
description: Mokokchung, situated in the eastern part of Nagaland, is a haven for adventure seekers and nature enthusiasts. The district is home to the Ao Naga tribe, known for their warm hospitality and vibrant culture. With its rolling hills, lush forests, and sparkling streams, Mokokchung offers a unique blend of natural beauty and tribal heritage. The town is surrounded by the Patkai range, providing endless opportunities for trekking, rock climbing, and exploring the great outdoors. Visitors can immerse themselves in the local culture by attending traditional festivals, visiting ancient villages, and sampling the region's exquisite cuisine. The district's rich biodiversity also makes it a haven for birdwatchers, with over 200 species of birds documented in the area.

name: Molungyimsen Historic Baptist Mission Site
description: Perched on a tranquil mountain ridge 50 km northwest of Mokokchung overlooking the Tuli valley, Molungyimsen is revered across Nagaland as the historic cradle of modern education and Christianity in the Naga Hills, founded on 24 October 1876 by American Baptist missionary Rev. Dr. E.W. Clark and his wife Mary Mead Clark along with 15 pioneering Ao Christian families, featuring Dr. Clark's preserved wooden bungalow, the historic prayer hall, the ancient litchi tree planted by Clark in 1878, and the first printing press site.

name: Mopungchuket Eco-Cultural Model Village
description: Situated 15 km north of Mokokchung town, celebrated as one of the cleanest, best-organized rural tourism villages in Northeast India, world-famous for the tragic 16th-century Romeo-and-Juliet romance of Jina and Etiben immortalized in stone monuments and a multi-tiered memorial watchtower, featuring the sacred Süngkotenem community forest park, a pristine village museum displaying ancient clan weapons and garments, and traditional wood-and-bamboo homestays.

name: Tangkum Marok Sacred Spring & Waterway
description: Located within the ancient historic territory of Ungma village in Mokokchung, Tangkum Marok is a revered perennial natural spring where crystal-pure water bubbles continuously from a subterranean rock aquifer. Steeped in ancestral Ao traditions, the spring has provided pure drinking water to village warriors and pilgrims for centuries, framed by stone steps, mossy boulders, and shaded mountain trees.

name: Tsumeya Tsuin Waterfall & Forest Gorge
description: Hidden within the dense subtropical mountain ravines of Mokokchung, Tsumeya Tsuin Waterfall is a pristine natural cascade where cold hill waters tumble down stepped granite rock shelves into a deep, jade-green plunge pool. Shaded by towering wild bamboo and fern trees, the site offers a tranquil, unspoiled wilderness retreat favored by local nature lovers.

name: Ungma Historic Ancestral Village
description: Situated 4 km south of Mokokchung town at an elevation of 1,325 meters, recognized as the oldest and largest village of the Ao Naga tribe, revered as the living ancestral museum of Ao culture from where clan branches migrated across the central hills, featuring monumental wood-carved bachelor dormitories (Morungs), massive hollowed-tree log drums beaten to announce ceremonies, the Baptist Centenary Memorial Church, and the scenic Babu Tsüba heritage park.

name: Aboi Town & Central Konyak Cultural Hub
description: Perched centrally on a windy mountain ridge 35 km southwest of Mon town, Aboi is an energetic sub-divisional hill town serving as the strategic geographical crossroads of the Konyak tribal homeland, celebrated for its vibrant weekly tribal bazaar where artisans from remote surrounding villages gather to barter hand-forged machetes (daos), brass necklaces, and hand-woven red-and-black Konyak textiles.

name: Chen Traditional Village & Skull Shrines
description: Situated in the remote eastern highland ridges of Mon district 45 km from Mon town near the Myanmar border, Chen (comprising Chen Wetnyu and Chen Moho) is an ancient Konyak settlement celebrated for preserving some of the most intact sacred headhunter skull shrines and ancient log drums in eastern Nagaland, where ancestral skulls recovered during 19th-century tribal conflicts were consecrated in natural stone rock shelters and venerated during seasonal fertility rituals.

name: Chui Traditional Village & Chief Angh's Mansion
description: Perched on a commanding hillock just 8 km from Mon town, Chui is a quintessential Konyak tribal village that meticulously preserves ancient architectural and social traditions, dominated by the colossal thatched palace of the village Angh, featuring a massive timber facade supported by tree-trunk pillars carved with figures of hornbills, warriors, and snakes, and interior courtyards displaying hundreds of historic buffalo and animal skull trophies accumulated across generations.

name: Hongphoi Village & Tattooed Konyak Warrior Heritage
description: Nestled in the misty hills close to Mon town, Hongphoi is a remarkably peaceful Konyak hamlet celebrated as one of the last living sanctuaries of the famed tattooed Konyak headhunter elders. The village preserves traditional bamboo longhouses, customary Angh royal compounds, and community courtyards where revered elders proudly display intricate facial and chest tattoo patterns earned in ancient warrior expeditions.

name: Longwa Traditional Village (Indo-Myanmar Border)
description: Perched on a high scenic mountain ridge 42 km east of Mon town, Longwa is celebrated worldwide as one of the most extraordinary geopolitical and cultural border settlements on Earth, where the international boundary between India and Myanmar runs right through the center of the village and bisects the vast thatched palatial residence of the hereditary Konyak Chief Angh (King) so that he sleeps in India and dines in Myanmar, home to surviving elderly tattooed Konyak headhunters, bronze gunsmiths, and opium-smoking elders.

name: Mon Village
description: Nestled amidst the tranquil hills of Nagaland, Mon Village is a nature lover's paradise that beckons adventure-seekers to explore its serene landscapes. With its rich cultural heritage, breathtaking vistas, and diverse wildlife, this trekking destination boasts a unique blend of history, geography, and natural beauty. The picturesque villages, lush forests, and sparkling waterfalls create an idyllic backdrop for trekkers to immerse themselves in the unspoiled beauty of Nagaland's Easternmost district.

name: Naginimora Historical Coal & Trading Outpost
description: Situated along the rocky banks of the Dikhu River on the border between Mon district and Sivasagar district of Assam, Naginimora ('Place of the Naga Queen's Grave') is an ancient border trading post celebrated in folklore for the historic burial place of an Ahom queen married to a Naga chieftain, transformed during the British colonial era in the 19th century into a major river trade and coal-depot hub for barging local coal down to the Brahmaputra River.

name: Phomching Village & Hilltop Fortification
description: Perched atop a rugged, high mountain ridge 20 km northeast of Mon town at an elevation of 1,400 meters, Phomching is a historic Konyak village that historically served as an impregnable natural military lookout and fortified mountain post, featuring an imposing traditional Angh's palace, wood-carved morungs, and breathtaking sweeping vantage points commanding views extending across the tea plains of Assam on one side and the misty ridges of Myanmar on the other.

name: Shangnyu Village & Sacred Monolithic Wooden Relief
description: Situated 25 km from Mon town, Shangnyu is an ancient royal Konyak settlement ruled by a powerful hereditary Angh, internationally celebrated by anthropologists for its extraordinary 8-foot-high, 12-foot-wide monolithic wooden relief carving panel preserved in the Angh's palace, revered in oral tradition as having been carved in ancient times by heavenly angels or spirits without human hands, depicting intricate cosmological motifs, human beings, tigers, pythons, hornbills, and celestial bodies.

name: Shengha Chingnyu Traditional Morungs & Woodcarvings
description: Perched on high mountain ridges in central Mon, Shengha Chingnyu is an ancient Konyak tribal village celebrated for its monumental bachelor dormitories (Morungs). These massive timber structures are adorned with intricate customary woodcarvings depicting hornbill birds, tigers, and ancestral skull reliefs, serving as living repositories of Konyak warrior traditions and clan oral lore.

name: Singphan Wildlife Sanctuary & Elephant Reserve Mon
description: Spanning over 23 square kilometers of dense, undisturbed tropical rainforest in the lower foothills of Mon district near Naginimora, Singphan Wildlife Sanctuary was officially notified as India's 30th Elephant Reserve. Contiguous with the Abhaypur Reserve Forest of Assam, this vital trans-border wildlife corridor is home to wild Asian elephants, leopards, hornbills, barking deer, wild boars, and a magnificent diversity of sub-Himalayan flora.

name: Tapi Riverbed & Traditional Suspension Bridges
description: Carving through the lush tropical rainforest valleys of southern Mon, the Tapi River is a crystal-clear mountain stream celebrated for pristine pebble shallows, deep turquoise fishing pools, and swaying cane-and-wire suspension footbridges that link remote Konyak hill hamlets across the gorge.

name: Tizit Valley & Konyak Tea Country Mon
description: Situated in the gentle fertile foothills along the Tizit River where the plains of Assam meet the rising hills of Mon district, Tizit serves as the commercial gateway to the Konyak homeland, celebrated for its expansive, emerald-green organic tea plantations, timber and plywood mills, scenic riverbed recreation spots along the Tizit River, and traditional Konyak villages perched on the surrounding hillocks.

name: Tobu Highland Mountain Station Mon
description: Perched on a lofty mountain shoulder at an altitude of 1,600 meters in southeastern Mon district near the border with Tuensang, Tobu is an atmospheric sub-divisional hill station renowned for its cool mountain climate, sweeping vistas of mist-draped mountain passes, traditional Konyak morungs adorned with ancient wood carvings, and vibrant celebrations of the Aoleang festival.

name: Veda Peak Viewpoint (Chui Ridge)
description: Standing as the highest geographical elevation in Mon district near Chui village, Veda Peak is a commanding mountain summit blanketed in wild sub-tropical orchids and moss-covered trees. On clear winter mornings, the summit provides an extraordinary dual vantage point: gaze westward across the vast Brahmaputra River plains of Assam, or eastward into the winding Chindwin River basin in Myanmar.

name: Wakching Village & Historic Megalithic Stone Cists
description: Perched on an elevated mountain ridge in western Mon district 35 km from Mon town, Wakching is a historic Konyak village celebrated in colonial anthropological research (documented extensively by Austrian ethnologist Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf in the 1930s), renowned as the pioneer of the Konyak small-scale organic tea cultivation revolution, and celebrated for preserving ancient megalithic skull stone cists and warrior burial monuments.

name: Wangbao Village Mountain Cliff Paths
description: Perched on precipitous mountain cliffs in eastern Mon, Wangbao is an offbeat Konyak village surrounded by terraced cardamom plantations, sweet orange orchards, and dramatic cliff paths. Narrow unpaved walking trails wind along sheer mountain ridges shrouded in drifting mountain fog, offering spectacular viewpoints over deep river canyons rolling into the border hills.

name: Hakhezhe Amur Falcon Roosting Grounds
description: Located among the extensive teak, rubber, and mixed forestry plantations of Hakhezhe village in Niuland, this rural woodland sanctuary serves as a major annual stopover and roosting corridor for tens of thousands of migratory Amur falcons (Falco amurensis) during their trans-continental flight from Siberia to Southern Africa between October and November.

name: Hevishe Village Community Museum (Niuland)
description: Preserved with immense pride by the villagers of Hevishe in central Niuland, this community-managed cultural museum houses an authentic ethnographic collection representing the Sumi Naga heritage. The display features ancient warrior spears, ceremonial daos, wild boar tusk headdresses, brass ornaments, antique handlooms, and traditional bamboo hunting traps donated by village clans.

name: Innatoli & Hozukhe Forest Edge Trails
description: Winding gently through the transitional foothills connecting Innatoli and Hozukhe villages in southern Niuland, these unpaved forest-edge trails traverse rich subtropical lowland forests, rubber plantations, and open grazing meadows. The corridor is rich in native birdlife, wild orchids, and medicinal flora, providing a peaceful escape for cycling and leisurely walking.

name: Lavi Lake & Wetland Community Reserve
description: Officially highlighted on the Niuland District Administration's portal, Lavi Lake is a tranquil natural freshwater lake set amidst fertile agricultural plains and rolling green hills. The lake features lotus-covered shallows, clean banks shaded by weeping willows, and community-managed fishing zones that attract nature enthusiasts and anglers seeking weekend respite.

name: Choklangan & Pangsha Frontier Mountain Ridges
description: Perched on knife-edge mountain ridges along the international border in eastern Noklak, Choklangan and Pangsha are dramatic frontier settlements commanding dizzying vistas. Looking eastward from these high-altitude ridges, the land plunges into deep, cloud-filled valleys that stretch into the untamed mountains of northwestern Myanmar, fringed by wild rhododendrons and sub-alpine flora.

name: Khao/Kholam Subterranean Caves (Noklak)
description: Hidden deep in the dense mountain forests of the Khiamniungan hills near Noklak, the Khao and Kholam caves form an extensive natural subterranean rock shelter system. Carved into limestone cliffs, the caves feature hidden tunnel chambers and natural defense portals that were historically used by ancestral tribal warriors as emergency shelters and strategic military outposts during inter-village battles.

name: Lang Riverbed Shallows & Forest Defile
description: Winding through deep forested ravines in central Noklak, the Lang River is celebrated for its pristine, icy-cold mountain waters that crash through narrow granite defiles into wide pebble shallows. Shaded by dense bamboo stands and tropical hardwood canopies, the river provides idyllic settings for wild camping, stream wading, and nature exploration.

name: Nokhu Village & Frontier Ridge Noklak
description: Perched atop a narrow, windy mountain ridge 18 km from Noklak town overlooking Myanmar, Nokhu is an ancient Khiamniungan tribal village renowned for its dramatic geographical setting, traditional wooden bachelor morungs supported by carved timber posts, ancient hollowed-tree log drums, and panoramic vantage points that look out directly over the rugged mountains of northwestern Myanmar.

name: Noklak Frontier Town & Khiamniungan Brasscraft Center
description: Perched on an elevated mountain ridge in the far eastern frontier of Nagaland bordering Myanmar 60 km east of Tuensang, Noklak is the district headquarters of the Khiamniungan Naga tribe, celebrated across the region as the center of ancient traditional brass and bell-metal casting (producing exquisite warrior neck torcs and bracelets using lost-wax methods), intricate cane armor and rain-shields, and the lively Tsokum and Khaozaosie-Hok-Ah tribal festivals.

name: Noklak Morung & Ancestral Megalith Trails
description: Scattered across the traditional settlement quarters of Noklak town and adjoining hamlets, this cultural heritage trail connects ancient stone menhirs, ancestral warrior seating platforms, and historic wood-carved bachelor dormitories (Morungs) housing monumental log drums. These sacred markers chronicle the oral history, clan alliances, and traditional spiritual beliefs of the Khiamniungan tribe.

name: Pangsha Border Village & Historic Trade Trails
description: Perched on a high ridge overlooking Myanmar in Noklak district 30 km from Noklak town (comprising Old Pangsha and New Pangsha), celebrated in colonial military history as the site of significant 1936 British punitive expeditions, famous today as a peaceful, vibrant Indo-Myanmar border trade outpost where Khiamniungan Nagas from both sides of the frontier meet at the Dan International Border Trade Center to trade hand-forged tools, textiles, and mountain produce.

name: Panso Highland Town & Cane Works Noklak
description: Perched on an elevated mountain ridge in Noklak district 25 km from Noklak town, Panso is an ancient Khiamniungan settlement renowned as a traditional center of indigenous metallurgy and cane craftsmanship, celebrated for master craftsmen who hand-cast brass warrior bracelets, torcs, and smoking pipes, as well as tightly woven cane chest protectors and defensive rain shields.

name: Thonoknyu & Chentang Saddle Viewpoint
description: Perched at an elevation of nearly 2,000 meters in southern Noklak district along the border with Shamator and Kiphire, Thonoknyu and the dramatic Chentang Saddle (locally called 'C-Saddle') form a breathtaking high-altitude mountain pass, renowned among adventure travelers for offering sweeping, unobstructed aerial panoramas extending deep into the Chindwin River valley of Myanmar, cool alpine breezes, and traditional Khiamniungan villages with wood-and-thatch architecture.

name: Wansoi Historic Khiamniungan Village
description: Perched on a lofty, windy mountain spur 15 km from Noklak town, Wansoi is an ancient Khiamniungan village renowned for its remarkably preserved tribal antiquity, featuring massive stone clan gates guarded by wooden figures, centuries-old hollowed log drums that can be heard miles across valleys, ancestral morungs with skull altars from pre-Christian eras, and master artisans who weave impenetrable defensive cane armor jackets.

name: Wui Village Handcrafted Traditional Blacksmithies
description: Perched on rugged mountain slopes in Noklak district, Wui is an ancient Khiamniungan Naga village renowned across the region as the historic metallurgical capital of the eastern hills. For centuries without modern machinery or electricity, village master blacksmiths have used manual goat-skin bellows and stone anvils over charcoal hearths to forge traditional warrior spears, ceremonial daos, and agricultural implements prized for durability.

name: Athibung Foothill Cultural Crossroads
description: Situated in the lower forested foothills of southwestern Peren district 40 km from Jalukie, Athibung is a vibrant sub-divisional center celebrated as a historic cultural confluence where the traditions of the Kuki and Zeliang tribes intertwine, famous for its sprawling natural bamboo groves, skilled cane basket weavers, the colorful Mim Kut post-harvest festival, and scenic river trails leading toward the Assam border.

name: Benreu
description: Benreu, a picturesque village in Nagaland, is a trekker's haven surrounded by lush forests, rolling hills, and majestic mountains. The region is home to the vibrant Ao Naga tribe, known for their rich cultural heritage and warm hospitality. As you trek through the dense forests and rugged terrain, you'll discover an array of exotic flora and fauna, including rare bird species and medicinal plants. The village offers breathtaking views of the surrounding landscape, with the majestic Saramati mountain range towering in the distance. Visitors can immerse themselves in the local culture by attending traditional festivals, interacting with the villagers, and sampling the delicious local cuisine.

name: Duilumreu Mini Hydro Scenic Viewpoint (Poilwa)
description: Situated in the pristine highlands near Poilwa village, the Duilumreu stream valley is a picturesque eco-tourism spot where a gushing mountain river has been harnessed through an eco-friendly mini hydroelectric weir. The surrounding ravine features dramatic cascading torrents, stone footbridges, and elevated view platforms overlooking deep forested gorges blanketed in subtropical pine and bamboo.

name: Jalukie Agricultural Valley & Rice Bowl
description: Nestled in a vast, fertile intermontane basin framed by the majestic Barail mountains 50 km from Dimapur, Jalukie is celebrated as the premier agricultural hub and 'Rice Bowl of Nagaland', characterized by thousands of acres of lush, green irrigated paddy flats, commercial organic horticulture farms producing watermelons, papayas, and king chillies, and home to the College of Veterinary Sciences and Animal Husbandry.

name: Mount Pauna (Pauna Peak) & Sacred Ridge
description: Rising majestically to an altitude of 2,841 meters (9,321 feet) in the Barail mountain range above Benreu village in Peren district, celebrated as the third highest mountain peak in Nagaland, revered in Zeliang tribal cosmology as a sacred mountain abode of benevolent spirits, renowned for its dense virgin dwarf-bamboo forests, rare alpine medicinal herbs, wild rhododendron groves, and a challenging mountain trek culminating in sensational vistas overlooking Manipur and the Assam plains.

name: Ngwalwa Village & Community Biodiversity Reserve
description: Situated 25 km north of Peren town along the scenic ridge route connecting Peren with Medziphema, Ngwalwa is a historic Zeliang village celebrated for its community-led environmental conservation, where the village council has declared hundreds of acres of ancient oak and rhododendron forest as a Community Biodiversity Reserve, banning hunting and commercial logging to protect hornbills, civets, and endemic orchid species.

name: Nsong & Kebai-Khelma Remote Ridge
description: Situated in the far western mountain frontier of Peren district bordering the Dima Hasao district of Assam, Nsong and the Kebai-Khelma region represent one of the most rugged and remote wilderness landscapes in Nagaland, celebrated by adventure enthusiasts for its challenging dirt tracks and 4x4 off-road trails winding through virgin bamboo jungles, deep river canyons, and traditional Zeme villages practicing shifting and terrace cultivation.

name: Ntangki (Intanki) National Park
description: Spanning 202.02 square kilometers in the southwestern corner of Peren district along the Dhansiri River basin, gazetted as a National Park in 1993, recognized as the solitary national park in the state of Nagaland, preserving one of the last contiguous stretches of virgin sub-tropical semi-evergreen and moist deciduous rainforests in the region, celebrated as a crucial refuge for the endangered Hoolock Gibbon, Clouded Leopard, Asian Elephant, Gaur (Mithun ancestor), Slow Loris, White-winged Wood Duck, and Great Indian Hornbill.

name: Pedi Waterfall & Subtropical Forest Trail
description: Hidden deep in the subtropical evergreen jungle near Pedi village in Peren, Pedi Waterfall is a pristine natural cascade where clear hill waters tumble over steep, mossy rock steps into a refreshing natural rock pool. Enclosed by giant ferns, wild banana groves, and singing cicadas, the spot offers an idyllic nature retreat along traditional village footpaths.

name: Poilwa Village & Snail-Trout Festival Grounds
description: Perched on a scenic mountain ridge in Peren district between Khonoma and Benreu at an altitude of 1,600 meters, Poilwa is a historic Zeliangrong tribal settlement renowned across Nagaland as the ancestral cradle of master cane and bamboo basketry, celebrated for its sparkling mountain streams that harbor fresh river snails and hill trout, and host to the annual Poilwa Snail and Trout Festival which showcases indigenous culinary delicacies.

name: Rani Gaidinliu Cave Complex (Puilwa)
description: Located in the rugged limestone hills near Puilwa village in Peren, this historic cavern complex served as an operational sanctuary, planning headquarters, and spiritual retreat for the iconic freedom fighter Rani Gaidinliu during her armed resistance against British colonial forces in the 1930s. The caves feature spacious subterranean chambers, natural rock ledges, and secret lookout portals overlooking deep forest ravines.

name: Teipuiki River Banks & Valley Boulder Gorge
description: Rushing through the deep mountain defiles of central Peren, the Teipuiki River is an untouched sub-Himalayan waterway characterized by foaming rapids, broad gravel flats, and colossal smooth granite boulders. Shaded by dense subtropical bamboo and evergreen forests, the riverbed is celebrated locally for angling mountain fish and peaceful riverside day camps.

name: Tening Town & Barail Mountain Ridge
description: Perched on a high windy mountain ridge at an elevation of 1,500 meters in southwestern Peren district near the border with Assam and Manipur, Tening is an atmospheric hill station serving as the administrative and cultural hub of the Liangmai and Zeme Naga communities, famous for its dramatic cloud scapes, cool alpine climate, terraced ginger and cardamom cultivation, and breathtaking panoramic vantage points overlooking the rugged Barail mountain spine.

name: Chizami Village & Indigenous Heritage Center
description: Perched on a scenic ridge in Phek district 85 km from Kohima along the highway to Tuensang, Chizami is celebrated globally as a pioneering model village of grassroots community transformation, led by the North East Network (NEN), renowned for reviving indigenous cotton cultivation and backstrap loin-loom weaving ('Chizami Weaves'), preserving over 25 varieties of traditional heirloom millets and seeds in community seed banks, and promoting gender equality.

name: Chozuba Terraced Ridge & Historic Morungs
description: Perched on an undulating mountain ridge in central Phek district 75 km east of Kohima, Chozuba is a historic sub-divisional hill town of the Chakhesang Nagas, renowned for its dramatic amphitheatre-like terraced rice fields that wrap around mountain shoulders, monumental stone monoliths commemorating ancient warrior exploits, traditional wood-carved morungs, and vibrant Sekrenyi festival celebrations.

name: Kapamodzü Peak Zhavame
description: Rising to an altitude of 2,620 meters (8,596 feet) above Zhavame village 16 km from Pfütsero, celebrated as the highest table-top mountain peak in Phek district, famous across the region for its expansive high-altitude grassy meadows that transform seasonally into vibrant carpets of wild yellow buttercups in summer and cherry blossoms and rhododendrons in winter, offering sweeping panoramic views across Mount Saramati and the Manipur valley.

name: Khezhakeno Village & Chida Resort Lake
description: Perched at an elevation of 1,660 meters on the southern border of Phek district 48 km from Kohima, revered in oral history across Nagaland as the legendary ancestral mother village from which all major Naga tribes (Tenyi-mia, Angami, Chakhesang, Lotha, Sema) dispersed, celebrated for the sacred stone slab 'Tsoh Ta' where paddy spread in the morning magically doubled by evening, and the scenic Chida Post Resort located 4 km uphill on the Indo-Myanmar border ridge featuring a mirror-like artificial lake.

name: Kikruma Historic Warrior Village Phek
description: Perched on a commanding rocky mountain promontory 15 km from Pfütsero in Phek district at an elevation of 1,650 meters, Kikruma is celebrated in colonial military history as the site of the fierce Battle of Kikrüma fought on 11-12 February 1851 against the British East India Company under Captain John Butler, renowned for its massive ancient stone ramparts, clan gate monoliths, centuries-old wood-carved morungs, and extensive irrigated terraced rice fields.

name: Luda & Zanibu Ridge High-Altitude Treks
description: Soaring above the southern agricultural valleys of Phek district near Zhavame, the Luda and Zanibu mountain ridges form a magnificent high-elevation trekking corridor. The ridges are blanketed in dense sub-alpine mossy forests, giant blooming rhododendrons, alpine dwarf bamboo, and rare medicinal herbs, offering sweeping vistas across the Manipur-Nagaland border mountains.

name: Meluri Town & Pochury Cultural Center
description: Perched on a commanding mountain ridge in eastern Phek district 160 km from Kohima at an elevation of 1,200 meters near the Myanmar border, Meluri is the ancestral cultural and administrative headquarters of the Pochury Naga tribe, celebrated for the grand Yemshe Festival (the premier harvest and community festival celebrated every October with ancient fire rituals and feasts), distinctive red-black Pochury shawls, and cane basketry.

name: Pfutsero
description: Pfutsero, situated in the Phek district of Nagaland, is a quaint town surrounded by lush green forests, rolling hills, and meandering streams. The region is steeped in rich cultural heritage, with the Chakhesang and Pochuri tribes inhabiting the area. As a trekker's haven, Pfutsero offers breathtaking vistas, diverse wildlife, and an array of adventure activities, making it an ideal destination for those seeking an immersive experience amidst nature. With its pleasant climate and serene ambiance, Pfutsero is a perfect getaway for travelers seeking to escape the chaos of city life and connect with the natural world.

name: Pfutsero Glory Peak & Paragliding Ridge
description: Perched at a cold, high altitude of 2,133 meters (7,000 feet) on a mountain ridge 65 km southeast of Kohima, Pfütsero is celebrated as the highest altitude town and coldest inhabited settlement in Nagaland (where temperatures frequently dip below freezing in December-January), famous for 'Glory Peak' offering breathtaking unobstructed vistas of Mount Saramati and Mount Everest on crystal-clear winter mornings, flourishing kiwi and apple orchards, and premier paragliding launching cliffs.

name: Phokhungri Border Highland & Rock Shelters
description: Perched on a windy mountain ridge on the far eastern international border with Myanmar in Meluri subdivision, Phokhungri is celebrated by archaeologists and off-road explorers as one of Nagaland's most remote frontier highland settlements, famous for ancient prehistoric limestone rock shelters and caves (specifically researched in the state archaeological study 'Cave Archaeology of Shilloi Lake and Phokhungri Areas'), virgin forests, and traditional Pochury culture.

name: Phusachodu Village & Eco-Trekking Trail
description: Situated on a lofty mountain spur 14 km from Pfütsero in Phek district, Phusachodu is celebrated as one of the largest and most populous ancestral villages of the Chakhesang Naga tribe, famous for its rich martial history, imposing stone clan gates, sweeping terrace fields, and a dedicated eco-tourism destination development project completed by the Department of Tourism featuring a marked trekking trail through fragrant pine ridges and mountain viewpoints.

name: Razeba Terraced Mountain Basin Phek
description: Nestled in a verdant, high-altitude mountain basin 18 km south of Pfütsero beneath the towering cliffs of Kapamodzü peak, Razeba is celebrated as one of Nagaland's most productive organic agricultural valleys, famous for its thousands of acres of stepped cabbage, potato, and garlic terrace farms that shimmer green against the mountain backdrop, traditional wooden granaries, and sparkling mountain streams.

name: Rüzazho Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Heritage House
description: Located in the historic Chakhesang village of Rüzazho in Phek district, this commemorated heritage house served as the operational headquarters of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and the Indian National Army (INA) in May 1944 during the Battle of Kohima. Officially recognized as the first village administered by the Azad Hind government in India, the site preserves Netaji's residence, historical wartime photographs, and patriotic commemorative plaques.

name: Sedzu Riverbed Shallows & Pebble Camping Banks
description: Flowing through a scenic mountain valley in central Phek, the Sedzu River is celebrated for wide, clean pebble beaches, calm crystalline shallows, and gentle river bends framed by terraced paddy fields and pine-clad hills. The riverbanks are a favored seasonal camping and cooking retreat for local Chakhesang youths and visiting outdoor enthusiasts.

name: Shilloi Lake (Lachem Lake) Meluri
description: Nestled in a picturesque valley basin among the pine-clad Patkai hills of Meluri subdivision near the international border with Myanmar 260 km from Kohima, celebrated as the largest natural freshwater lake in Nagaland, spanning an area of 0.25 to 0.30 square kilometers, shaped distinctively like a giant human footprint, revered by the indigenous Pochury Nagas as sacred water protected by spirits (who strictly forbid bathing or washing), surrounded by weeping willows and migratory Siberian waterfowl.

name: Tso Tawo Mythological Lake & Stone Sites (Khezhakeno)
description: Located in the legendary ancestral village of Khezhakeno in western Phek, Tso Tawo is a sacred mythological flat stone slab and accompanying natural water pool steeped in indigenous Naga creation lore. According to ancient oral traditions, paddy spread over this magical stone slab would double by sunset, leading to the early prosperity and eventual migration of ancestral tribes across the Naga highlands.

name: Wazeho Limestone Hills & Mineral Valley
description: Nestled in a remote, picturesque mountain valley in Meluri subdivision near the Myanmar border 45 km beyond Meluri town, Wazeho is celebrated for its dramatic landscape of white sedimentary limestone bluffs, natural karst springs, and the historic Wazeho Mini Cement Plant (established by the Nagaland State Mineral Development Corporation), surrounded by dense pine forests and unexplored speleological caves.

name: Zhavame Vegetable Bowl & Flower Haven
description: Nestled in a verdant mountain amphitheatre at the foot of Kapamodzü peak 12 km from Pfütsero, Zhavame is an enchanting Chakhesang tribal village celebrated as one of Nagaland's most productive organic horticultural settlements, famous for its colossal terraced cabbage, potato, and garlic fields, traditional stone-and-wood granaries, and the vibrant Kapamodzü and Zhavame Flower Festival celebrating the blooming of wild alpine cherry blossoms.

name: Aunglung (Lovers' Double Boulder Formation)
description: Perched on a scenic ridge near Shamator town, Aunglung is a pair of colossal natural limestone boulders that lean intimately toward each other. In indigenous Yimkhiung folklore, these twin stones immortalize two ancient star-crossed lovers whose spirits were eternally bonded in stone by the deities, surrounded by panoramic views of the Saramati mountain foothills.

name: Chessore Heritage Village & Log Drum House
description: Perched on a high mountain saddle commanding dramatic views of the surrounding valleys, Chessore is an ancient Yimkhiung Naga ancestral village. The village preserves monumental hand-hewn wooden log drums housed in traditional timber morungs, stepped terraced rice fields cascading into deep gorges, and customary clan council institutions that uphold centuries of folk traditions.

name: Kinihung Heritage Ridge & Saramati Foothill Trail
description: Stretching along a panoramic mountain spine in eastern Shamator, the Kinihung Heritage Ridge trail provides high-altitude trekking paths through sub-tropical pine and oak groves. The elevated ridge delivers unbroken vistas of Mount Saramati—Nagaland's tallest peak—and the sweeping border ranges rolling into Myanmar.

name: Likimro River Rapids & Mountain Gorge
description: Rushing through deep rocky gorges in southern Shamator, the Likimro River is an untamed mountain waterway characterized by roaring white-water rapids, crystal turquoise deep pools, and sheer forested canyon walls. The river corridor provides pristine habitats for native hill fishes and serves as an exhilarating destination for river trekking and wilderness camping.

name: Shamator Town & Yimkhiung Cultural Heartland
description: Perched on an elevated mountain ridge in eastern Nagaland 55 km south of Tuensang at an altitude of 1,500 meters, Shamator is the district headquarters of the Yimkhiung Naga tribe, celebrated as the epicenter of Yimkhiung cultural identity, famous for the vibrant annual Medhü Festival (celebrated with warrior hornbill-feather dances, communal feasting, and peace rituals), traditional cane and bamboo weaving, and panoramic views of the Saramati mountain range.

name: Tsungketshir Natural Limestone Caves (Chessore)
description: Tucked away in the forested hills near Chessore in Shamator district, Tsungketshir is a subterranean limestone cavern system featuring spacious underground chambers, natural rock pillars, and crystalline dripstone formations. The grottos were historically used by Yimkhiung warriors as emergency defensive shelters and scouting stations.

name: Gwasinlo Forest Stream & Shallows
description: Flowing through a sheltered forested valley near Gwasinlo village in northern Tseminyu, this crystal-clear mountain brook is characterized by smooth water-sculpted stone basins, calm gravel shallows, and lush banks blanketed in wild banana groves and bamboo clumps. The stream is a beloved local retreat for nature walks, freshwater wading, and seasonal family picnics.

name: Khinrun (Governor's View Point Tseminyu)
description: Perched on a prominent high-altitude ridge near Tseminyu town, Khinrun—widely known locally as Governor's View Point—is a scenic summit celebrated for panoramic mountain vistas. Historically favored by visiting dignitaries and governors, the lookout provides sweeping views across the layered mountain ranges of central Nagaland, with early morning mist blanketing the agricultural valleys below.

name: Ngada Cultural Festival Grounds (Tseminyu)
description: Situated in the civic heart of Tseminyu, the Ngada Cultural Festival Grounds serve as the traditional arena for the annual Ngada festival—the grandest post-harvest celebration of the Rengma Naga community celebrated every November. The grounds feature a traditional amphitheater, ceremonial monoliths, carved wood pillars, and display pavilions where vibrant folk dances, choral music, and customary reconciliation rites are conducted.

name: Sendenyu Biodiversity Base Camp & Field Station
description: Located at the gateway to the Sendenyu Community Biodiversity and Wildlife Reserve, this eco-field station serves as a model educational center for community-led biodiversity conservation. Managed by village youth and elders, the base camp features wildlife interpretation displays, guided nature trailheads into virgin oak-laurel forests, birding hides, and rustic eco-camps frequented by researchers and eco-travelers.

name: Sendenyu Community Biodiversity Conservation Area
description: Spanning 12 square kilometers of rugged, virgin mountain forest in Tseminyü district 18 km west of Tseminyü town, established in 2001 by a landmark resolution of the Sendenyu Village Council, celebrated across India as a pioneering model of indigenous community biodiversity conservation, where the villagers enacted customary conservation laws and created a wildlife corridor protecting the Great Indian Hornbill, Barking Deer, Wild Boar, Leopard Cat, and rare medicinal flora.

name: Terogvunyu Hillock Viewpoints & Terraced Vistas
