description: Perched on gentle pine-crested hillocks near Terogvunyu village in Tseminyu district, these scenic viewpoints command breathtaking vistas over the undulating agricultural heartland of the Rengma tribe. The hillsides are carved with ancient terraced rice fields that gleam emerald-green during the monsoon and golden during winter harvest, framed by distant blue mountain ranges.

name: Tseminyü Town & Rengma Cultural Heartland
description: Situated on a scenic mountain ridge 50 km north of Kohima along National Highway 2, Tseminyü is the newly created district headquarters and ancestral cultural capital of the Rengma Naga tribe, historically renowned for having introduced iron blacksmithing and metallurgy to the Naga hills, celebrated for the colorful annual Ngada Festival (an eight-day post-harvest festival in late November featuring traditional warrior chants, fire rituals, and feasting), and traditional Rengma woven shawls (Rikhyü).

name: Changsangmon Historical Ancestral Settlement
description: Perched on a high rocky promontory in Tuensang district, Changsangmon is celebrated in Chang oral history and folklore as the ancestral mother settlement where the Chang Naga people lived as an undivided community following their migration from Chungliyimti, renowned for its ancient defensive stone ramparts, sacred monoliths erected by founding clan patriarchs, and archaeological traces of ancient round stone-paved meeting platforms.

name: Chingmei Village & Ancient Stone Defensive Walls
description: Perched on a commanding mountain ridge in southern Tuensang, Chingmei is an ancient Chang Naga settlement celebrated for historical fortifications. The village preserves centuries-old defensive stone perimeter walls, massive wooden village gates, traditional clan Morung dormitories housing monumental log drums, and oral histories recounting historic warrior expeditions.

name: Chungliyimti Historical Origin Site
description: Situated on a mystical, wind-swept mountain ridge 20 km east of Mokokchung along the border with Tuensang district, celebrated in the oral mythology of the Ao, Sangtam, and Chang Naga tribes as their sacred ancestral point of genesis, famous for 'Lungterok' (literally 'Six Stones' - six ancient monolithic stones protruding from the earth from which, according to tribal cosmology, the original three male and three female human ancestors emerged into the world), stone battlements, and ancient seed-grinding stones.

name: Livingstone (Naklak) Waterfall & Forest Pool
description: Tucked away in the dense, subtropical mountain forests near Tuensang, Livingstone Waterfall (also known locally as Naklak Waterfall) is an unpolluted natural cascade where clear mountain water plunges over sheer granite cliff shelves into a tranquil jade-green plunge pool. Shaded by wild bamboo canopies and towering mountain trees, the waterfall offers an idyllic nature sanctuary.

name: Longterok Ancient Six-Stone Emergence Site
description: Situated within the sacred historic grounds of Chungliyimti in Tuensang, Longterok (literally 'Six Stones' in the Ao language) is a revered natural geological stone formation. According to ancient indigenous creation myths, the ancestral progenitors of the Ao, Lotha, and Phom Naga tribes emerged from these six sacred stones, making it the foundational legendary cradle of indigenous hill civilization in central Nagaland.

name: Noksen Historic Baptist Church & Village
description: Situated on a scenic mountain saddle in Tuensang district 30 km north of Tuensang town along the road to Longleng, Noksen is an ancient Chang tribal village renowned as the early spiritual cradle of Christian mission work in eastern Nagaland, celebrated for its historic mission church selected by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India under the PRASHAD pilgrimage tourism circuit, traditional stone-carved village gates, and sweeping views of the Dikhu river valley.

name: Panso & Yokao Foothill Paths & Terrace Fields
description: Winding across elevated foothill valleys connecting Panso and Yokao villages, these undisturbed rural paths traverse magnificent terraced rice paddies carved into steep mountain slopes. Flanked by crystal streams, bamboo copses, and wildflower hedges, the trails offer breathtaking views of traditional agrarian landscapes.

name: Tsadang Rock Caves & Natural Waterfall
description: Located in the rugged hills near Tsadang village in Tuensang, this picturesque natural site combines ancient rock shelters with a gushing perennial mountain cascade. The caves, tucked behind curtains of hanging vines and wild ferns, feature natural stone benches historically used by traveling traders and hunters.

name: Tuensang Town & Chang Tribal Cultural Center
description: Perched on a sprawling mountain ridge in eastern Nagaland 110 km from Mokokchung at an elevation of 1,371 meters, Tuensang is celebrated as the largest and most historic urban hill station in eastern Nagaland, historically serving as the headquarters of the Tuensang Frontier Division during British and NEFA administration, recognized as the vibrant cultural crossroads where the Chang, Sangtam, and Yimkhiung tribes converge, famous for the grand Naknyulüm and Poanglem tribal festivals.

name: Baghty Passion Fruit Valley & Agro-Country
description: Stretching across the fertile foothill valley of western Wokha, Baghty is celebrated as the passion fruit capital of Nagaland. Rolling hillsides are blanketed in vast organic plantations of yellow and purple passion fruit vines, orange groves, and tea gardens, supporting thriving local agro-processing units and scenic valley farm walks.

name: Bhandari Foothill Valley & Mineral Belt Wokha
description: Situated in the gentle fertile foothills of western Wokha district bordering the Golaghat district of Assam, Bhandari is a scenic sub-divisional center celebrated for its vast organic orange, passion fruit, and rubber plantations, historical significance as an early oil exploration and hydrocarbon reserve corridor of Nagaland, and tranquil rural Lotha settlements nestled along foothill streams.

name: Chukitong Ridge & Valley Viewpoint
description: Perched on a narrow, breezy mountain saddle along National Highway 2 between Wokha and Mokokchung 16 km north of Wokha town at an elevation of 1,400 meters, Chukitong is an idyllic hill station celebrated for its elevated roadside viewpoints that command sensational panoramic vistas overlooking the winding Doyang River gorge, lush green terraced hillsides, rolling clouds, and traditional Lotha wood-and-tin village dwellings.

name: Doyang Hydro Project & Reservoir
description: Constructed across the Doyang River in Wokha district by the North Eastern Electric Power Corporation (NEEPCO), celebrated as Nagaland's largest hydroelectric project with an installed capacity of 75 megawatts, creating an immense, breathtaking sapphire-blue water reservoir that snakes through forested green hillocks, highlighted in the state tourism policy as eastern India's premier destination for river sports, speed boating, freshwater angling, and world-famous birdwatching.

name: Englan Range Eco-Tourism & Trekking Ridge
description: Situated across the rolling mountain ranges of northern Wokha district 18 km from Wokha town, Englan Range is a dedicated eco-tourism destination developed by the Department of Tourism, Government of Nagaland, celebrated for its dense semi-evergreen forests, terraced organic orange and passion-fruit orchards, panoramic trekking routes along mountain spines, and comfortable eco-cottages managed by local youth eco-clubs.

name: Etsüchukha Sacred Spring Pool & Lotha Grove
description: Located in a serene wooded ravine on the edge of Wokha town, Etsüchukha is an ancient natural freshwater spring pool that has sustained the town for generations. Enclosed by massive centuries-old sacred trees, stone masonry steps, and lush mossy rocks, the pool is revered in local Lotha traditions as a symbol of perpetual life and communal harmony.

name: Liphanyan Governor's Camp & Doyang River Meanders
description: Situated along a scenic, meandering stretch of the lower Doyang River near Liphanyan village, Governor's Camp is a historic wilderness campsite favored since colonial times by visiting dignitaries. The riverbank features expansive white sandbars, calm turquoise river pools, and dense tropical hardwood forests, making it one of the premier spots in Wokha for river rafting, wilderness camping, and angling.

name: Mount Tiyi (Tiyi Peak) - Sacred Lotha Abode
description: Rising to an altitude of 1,970 meters (6,463 feet) above Wokha town, Mount Tiyi is celebrated as the sacred spiritual mountain of the Lotha Naga tribe, revered in ancient folklore as the mythical realm where the souls of departed ancestors dwell, adorned with natural orchards of wild rhododendrons, wild orchids, and mountain walnuts, featuring a scenic ridge trail culminating in breathtaking panoramic views of the Doyang river valley and eight districts of Nagaland on clear days.

name: Pangti Village & Amur Falcon Roosting Capital
description: Situated on the ridge above the Doyang reservoir in Wokha district, Pangti village is celebrated globally as the 'Falcon Capital of the World', world-famous for an extraordinary conservation revolution where local Lotha Naga hunters transformed into dedicated protectors, hosting over one million migrating Amur Falcons (Falco amurensis) every year in October and November as they make their epic trans-oceanic flight from eastern Siberia and northern China to Southern Africa.

name: Sungro Village & Doyang Aerial Viewpoint
description: Situated on a high mountain promontory 32 km from Wokha town overlooking the vast northern expanse of the Doyang reservoir, Sungro is a scenic Lotha tribal settlement renowned for offering the most spectacular elevated aerial vantage point overlooking the sapphire-blue waters of Doyang Lake winding through green mountain fingers, traditional Lotha timber homes, and tranquil orange orchards.

name: Totsu Wozhu Sacred Cliff Lake
description: Nestled secretly under the colossal rocky overhang of the Totsu Cliff near Wozhuro in Wokha district, Totsu Wozhu is an enchanting freshwater lake steeped in ancient Lotha mythology. Shrouded by dense subtropical forest and wild mountain orchids, the lake waters are held sacred in local lore as a divine sanctuary, offering an aura of mystical tranquility.

name: Tsungiki–Philimi Doyang Community Fishing Confluence
description: Situated at the scenic river confluence where the Doyang River carves between Tsungiki village in Wokha district and Philimi village in Zunheboto district, celebrated across Nagaland as a historic site of inter-tribal cultural harmony between the Lotha and Sumi Naga tribes, famous for the traditional biennial Tsungiki-Philimi Community Fishing Event, where thousands of villagers gather along the rocky banks to harvest river fish using indigenous root-bark extracts and woven wicker traps.

name: Vankhosung Baptist Mission Compound Wokha
description: Situated 4 km from Wokha town along the highway, established in the early 20th century as the spiritual and educational headquarters of the Lotha Baptist Churches Association (KBES), celebrated as the cradle of Christian faith and modern vernacular education for the Lotha Naga people, featuring a historic mission church, heritage mission bungalows, lush pine groves, and formally selected by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India under the national PRASHAD pilgrimage scheme.

name: Wokha
description: Wokha, the district headquarters of Wokha district in Nagaland, is a stunning destination nestled in the easternmost part of India. The region is known for its captivating landscape, with rolling hills, verdant forests, and meandering rivers that offer breathtaking views. With its rich cultural heritage and diverse wildlife, Wokha is a haven for adventure seekers and nature lovers alike. The district is home to the Lotha Naga tribe, who are known for their warm hospitality and vibrant traditions. Visitors can immerse themselves in the local culture by attending traditional festivals, visiting ancient villages, and sampling the region's unique cuisine. For the more adventurous, Wokha offers a range of outdoor activities, including trekking, rock climbing, and bird watching, making it an ideal destination for those seeking an adrenaline-packed vacation.

name: Aizuto Mission Compound Zunheboto
description: Perched on a quiet mountain ridge in Zunheboto district 15 km from Zunheboto town, Aizuto is celebrated as the historic mother mission compound of the Sümi Baptist Church, established in the early 20th century as the spiritual and educational center that brought literacy, healthcare, and Christianity to the Sümi Naga people, featuring a historic mission church, heritage colonial timber bungalows, and formally selected by the Ministry of Tourism under the national PRASHAD pilgrimage scheme.

name: Akuluto Town & Nagaland University Lumami Campus
description: Perched on rolling green mountain ridges 30 km south of Mokokchung at an elevation of 1,300 meters, Akuluto and adjacent Lumami form an intellectual and cultural hub in northern Zunheboto district, celebrated as the permanent residential headquarters campus of Nagaland University (the state's central university), featuring expansive hilltop academic complexes, botanical gardens, pine groves, and panoramic views of the surrounding central Naga hills.

name: Ghathashi Historic Sema Settlement & Valley
description: Nestled in a picturesque valley basin in southern Zunheboto district 45 km north of Kohima, Ghathashi is an ancient, historic settlement of the southern Sümi (Sema) Nagas, renowned for its extensive green irrigated terraced rice fields that fill the valley floor, traditional wooden clan gates, historic feast monoliths, and serving as the cultural cradle of the famous Thuwu-ni cultural festival.

name: Ghosu Bird Sanctuary & Community Forest Reserve
description: Nestled in the lush hills on the outskirts of Zunheboto town, Ghosu Bird Sanctuary is an exemplary community-managed forest reserve protected by local village elders and conservationists. The sanctuary harbors over 20 species of cuckoos, hornbills, hill partridges, babblers, and rare migratory birds amidst pristine subtropical broadleaf forest and natural salt licks.

name: Kizari Riverbed & Rapids (Zunheboto)
description: Flowing through an unspoiled mountain valley in southern Zunheboto, the Kizari River is celebrated for cold, clear waters rushing over granite rapids and broad gravel flats. Enclosed by dense oak and rhododendron forests, the riverbed is a favored local destination for catch-and-release angling, wilderness day camps, and stream hiking.

name: Pughoboto Sub-Divisional Hill Station
description: Perched on a high breezy mountain spur in southern Zunheboto district 55 km from Kohima at an elevation of 1,450 meters, Pughoboto is an atmospheric sub-divisional hill station renowned for its cool alpine climate, scenic pine woodlands, and as the host venue of the famous annual Thuwu-ni Festival (a vibrant three-day cultural, music, and indigenous sports extravaganza celebrating local youth empowerment, indigenous cuisine, and traditional wrestling).

name: Satoi Range Wildlife & Ecotourism Ridge
description: Rising majestically across the southeastern border of Zunheboto and Kiphire districts at altitudes exceeding 2,200 meters, the Satoi Range is celebrated as one of the last remaining contiguous primary virgin forests of central Nagaland, adorned with centuries-old giant rhododendron and oak canopies, rare wild mountain orchids, and recognized in the Nagaland Tourism Policy as a premier eco-tourism and birdwatching habitat harboring the vulnerable Blyth's Tragopan.

name: Sukhai & Kivikhu Eco-Trail Villages
description: Set amidst the rolling green highlands of western Zunheboto, Sukhai and Kivikhu are award-winning community eco-tourism hamlets celebrated for voluntary wildlife conservation. The villages feature guided forest eco-trails through protected community reserves, rich butterfly corridors, river eco-parks, and authentic traditional bamboo homestays operated by Sumi families.

name: Sumi Baptist Church Zunheboto (Asia's Largest Church Building)
description: Perched majestically atop the highest hillock in Zunheboto town at an elevation of 1,864 meters, the Sumi Baptist Church (SBCZ) is an architectural marvel recognized as the largest church building in Asia. Designed in a striking blue-domed octagonal shape, this monumental structure stands 166 feet tall and can seat over 8,500 worshippers in its main auditorium, offering magnificent 360-degree panoramas of the surrounding mountain ranges.

name: Suruhuto Highland Town & Oak Hills Zunheboto
description: Perched on a commanding mountain ridge at an elevation of 1,650 meters in northern Zunheboto district 20 km from Zunheboto town, Suruhuto is an atmospheric hill station of the Sümi Nagas, renowned for its cool bracing climate, surrounding virgin oak and rhododendron forests that bloom in spring, traditional Sümi wood-and-bamboo dwellings, and elevated viewpoints overlooking the Tizu River canyon.

name: Tizu River Biodiversity Corridor Zunheboto
description: Carving a deep, dramatic rocky canyon through central and eastern Nagaland before flowing into the Chindwin River of Myanmar, the Tizu River is celebrated in the Nagaland Tourism Policy as a premier water body for eco-tourism, river trekking, and sport angling, famous for the pioneering Chengu Community Biodiversity Conservation Area where local Sumi villages declared a 10-km stretch of the river as a no-fishing sanctuary to revive populations of the endangered Golden Mahseer and freshwater hill trout.

name: Zunheboto Town & Sümi Baptist Church
description: Perched on a commanding hillock at an elevation of 1,874 meters in central Nagaland, Zunheboto is the cultural heartland of the martial Sümi Naga tribe, world-famous for the monumental Sümi Baptist Church Zunheboto (SBAK) inaugurated in April 2017, recognized as one of the largest church buildings in Asia, standing 166 feet tall with a floor area of 23,735 square feet, seating 8,500 worshippers under a colossal egg-shaped blue dome with a 27-bell chime cast in Poland.

description: Perched on a strategic mountain crest in the far southeastern corner of Meluri district, Avakhung is an officially designated international border trade post connecting India with the Sagaing Region of Myanmar. The frontier outpost offers sweeping, unbroken vistas of the mist-shrouded mountain chains and deep forested valleys extending endlessly into Myanmar, serving as an important cultural and economic bridge for trans-border Pochury communities.
